--- title: "Pseudoword reading: one syllable" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · LEC_PSEUDO_1sil" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (C · Oral reading fluency; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea LEC_PSEUDO_1sil`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Lectura de pseudopalabras monosílabas*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/LEC_PSEUDO_1sil.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Pseudoword reading: one syllable, at age 6 (2,146 administrations in 2 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .75. AUC .92 against persistent difficulty (circular: the label uses this task). ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 70 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | reading aloud | | Items | 12 | | Task family | C · Oral reading fluency | | Score | Correct responses per minute | | Instructions (platform) | The child has 60 ss to read aloud words/pseudowords of increasing difficulty presented one by one on the screen. If the child says a wrong name or string, or delays more than 5ss, the answer is scored as error. | ## Theoretical framework Reading syllables, words and pseudowords aloud measures **written word recognition**: converting letters into sounds and accessing the word. It is the decoding component of the simple view of reading [@hoover1990simple] and the core of dyslexia according to the IDA definition (@sec-definicion). **What distinguishes each list.** Dual-route models separate two procedures. The **sublexical route** converts graphemes into phonemes and is the only one that works for pseudowords. The **lexical route** recognizes the whole word, and it shows in words being read faster than pseudowords (lexicality effect) and frequent words faster than rare ones. In Spanish, children use both from Grade 2 [@avdyli2014lexical; @davies2013lexical]. That is why the platform has both lists: pseudowords measure pure decoding, and the difference with words estimates how much orthographic lexicon the child has built. Length (from one to four syllables) makes serial reading visible: the more the child depends on letter-by-letter conversion, the more each added syllable costs. **In a transparent orthography, what discriminates is speed.** In Spanish, almost all children read accurately by the middle of Grade 1. Children with dyslexia are accurate but read more slowly, and their reading resembles that of younger children of the same reading level: it is delayed rather than deviant development [@davies2007spanish]. A meta-analysis of 79 European studies concludes that reading speed distinguishes readers with dyslexia in all orthographies and ages, whereas accuracy depends on age and transparency [@carioti2021depth]. In German, 70% of slow readers in Grade 1 were still slow in Year 8 [@landerl2008fluency]. That is why the score in these task sheets is **correct responses per minute**, not correct responses. **What our data show.** These are the most reliable and valid tasks on the platform: - **Reliability.** Stability between terms of ρ = .65 to .81, and 2021 α between .73 and .97. - **External validity.** They predict low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency years later with a median AUC of .72 to .77 ([chapter](../../criterio-woodcock.en.qmd)). The longer lists (three- and four-syllable words) predict best. - **Delay or deviance.** Comparing pseudowords with words among children of the same reading level separates delay from deviance ([Norms by reading level](../../baremo-nivel-lector.en.qmd)). ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 6.2| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 909| 262| 647| 34| | 6.2| 2012| 632|2018/19 | 315| 312| 0| 16| | 6.3| 2010| 160|2016/17 | 922| 256| 665| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness|% floor |% ceiling | |----------:|---:|----------:|-----:|-----:|------:|--------:|:-------|:---------| | 6.2| 574| 2010, 2012| 33.54| 16.51| 35.40| -0.36|NA |NA | | 6.3| 256| 2010| 40.74| 16.30| 42.81| -0.61|NA |NA | **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct items per minute). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 6.2| 574|0–65.0 |0–76.4 | | | 6.3| 256|0–70.0 |0–72.8 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .75 (median .75, 1 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .93. As a timed task, stability is the preferred reliability estimate. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2010| 6.2| 6.3| 886| 0.76| 0.75| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Word and text reading), r = .41–.92. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (6.2, r = .62); Reading comprehension (6.3, r = .40). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .92 (circular: agreement only). Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .58–.61. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_PSEUDO_1sil_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .37–.73 (2 time points; 268–331 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:|----:| | 6.2| 574| 2010, 2012| 0.0| 6.9| 16.7| 23.0| 35.4| 45.1| 54.0| | 6.3| 256| 2010| 3.7| 19.3| 25.4| 32.3| 42.8| 51.0| 60.4| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_LEC_PSEUDO_1sil_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 1,219| 0.134| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 1,215| -0.096| 0.093| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 1,210| 0.060| 0.036| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 1,224| 0.172| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.3| 922| 0.134| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.3| 920| -0.114| 0.086| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.3| 919| 0.059| 0.075| |School (ICC) | 6.3| 922| 0.130| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Pseudoword reading: one syllable” (code 70; LEEDUCA battery) assesses decoding (sublexical route). The child reads aloud the stimuli shown on the screen and the examiner records each correct response or error. It comprises 12 items. The time limit is 30 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010 and 2012 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 6 years of age. The main outcome is the efficiency (correct responses per unit of time). In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .93 (N = 319, 12 items). Because the task is timed, α tends to overestimate reliability; stability across administrations is the preferred estimate. Stability across time points was ρ = .75. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .58–.61. ## Pending issues - Estabilidad muy baja entre aplicaciones (ρ = -0.32): revisar los datos (códigos, versiones o tiempos) antes de usar la tarea *(Spanish)* - The persistent difficulty label uses this task: validity against it is circular. - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
